chapters.title: Chapter 13: Landmark Doctrines—Wi-LAN, Inc. v. Apple Inc.
chapters.reason: This chapter explicitly teaches the Federal Circuit's articulation of standards of review (JMOL, regional-circuit law application, and claim-construction review). Including key excerpts from the Wi‑LAN opinion will let students see the Court's precise framing and language that govern appellate review and explain the court's reversal.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Landmark Doctrines—Apple Inc. v. Wi-LAN Inc.
chapters.reason: The chapter focuses on the substantial-evidence standard as applied to infringement and damages. Quoting the Apple v. Wi‑LAN opinion is important so readers can analyze the Court's exact description of 'substantial evidence' and how it was applied to expert mappings and documentary support.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Landmark Doctrines—Johns Hopkins University v. Datascope Corp.
chapters.reason: This chapter teaches the doctrine that self‑contradictory expert testimony cannot sustain a verdict. Including the Datascope excerpts will show the controlling formulations and examples the Federal Circuit used to deem testimony legally insufficient.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Landmark Doctrines—Continental Circuits LLC v. Intel Corp.
chapters.reason: The chapter covers prosecution disclaimer and the 'clear and unambiguous' requirement. Excerpts from Continental Circuits are valuable to present the Court's precise standard and language distinguishing mere amendment from limiting disavowal.
